title: Introduce opportunistic batch merging and KV locality hinting to reduce small-batch tail latency
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Problem: We observe a persistent tail-latency and cost inflation for workloads composed of many small inference requests (single-turn queries, token-limited calls from mobile clients). The serving runtime currently favors strict batch boundaries which reduces jitter for large batches but leaves many small batches being dispatched immediately. These small batches cause inefficient kernel utilization and frequent KV cache lookups across shards, which raises both latency and GPU utilization.

Proposed work:
1) Opportunistic batch merging: implement a light-weight runtime layer that can merge small, compatible batches that arrive within a short opportunistic window (configurable, default 4ms) based on model compatibility, sequence-length bucket, and priority. This is not a general-purpose delay; it's designed to avoid adding latency for high-priority low-SLO traffic. The merge logic sits in the ingress/aggregator and emits merged batch descriptors to the existing batch execution pipeline.

2) KV locality hinting: augment request metadata with a locality hint (derived from token prefix hash + session affinity) that the KV cache sharding layer uses to favor local shard lookups and preferentially keep hot prefix entries in target shards. We'll add a hint propagation path that is cheap (metadata header), and a periodic background rebalance that moves a small percentage of hot entries per shard during low load.

3) Scheduler simplification: remove an old 3-lane priority split (urgent / normal / background) and replace with a two-tier admission token accounting model that simplifies preemption and clarifies SLO accounting. The new model exposes an admission token meter per tenant and a global opportunistic budget that the opportunistic merger draws from.

Scope & constraints: Must be safe for multi-tenant hosted deployments (no cross-tenant KV leaks), compatible with Dedicated and Private, and feature-flaggable for progressive rollout (start in canary region). We will not change model kernels or GPU memory layout. The change touches the ingress aggregator, KV sharding layer, scheduler admission path, and observability hooks.

Why unique / benefit: This approach reduces cost by increasing average batch size with minimal latency overhead for most traffic and reduces cross-shard KV fetches by keeping hot prefixes local, improving overall GPU utilization and decreasing tail. It also simplifies scheduler logic and makes admission budgets explicit for ops teams.
acceptance_criteria: Opportunistic merger feature-flagged behind runtime.config.opportunistic_merge (default off)
End-to-end canary deploy in us-west2 for 72h with rollback plan
Measured p99 request latency reduction >= 12% for small-batch synthetic workload (mean batch size before <= 2 tokens) in canary
KV cross-shard fetch rate reduced >= 20% for canary workloads after locality hinting enabled
No customer-visible KV leakage across tenants; pass automated multi-tenant integration tests
Scheduler token accounting API published in the console with per-tenant meters exposed in the dashboards
Migration and rollback playbook committed to Confluence and linked in PRs
notes: We will also take this opportunity to upgrade gRPC from 1.50.2 -> 1.56.0 in the serving runtime to pick up improvements in client-side async completion queuing. This requires a small change in our build matrix and a glidepath note for Dedicated customers; security team has pre-signed off on the version bump (see comment below).
comments: 2026-01-12 | Aisha Raman: Initial ticket. Captured observed symptom (small-batch tail) and drafted three-pronged approach: merge, hinting, scheduler simplification. Tagged Diego for grooming.

2026-01-14 | Diego Alvarez: Groomed with team. Risks noted: head-of-line blocking from merging, KV consistency during rebalance, and ensuring per-tenant fairness. Suggested conservative default windows and strict feature flags. Assigned estimate 8 points.

2026-01-19 | Priya Shah (SRE): SRE review: Request observability hooks (merge_count, merged_batch_size_histogram, kv_rebalance_ops). Require alert when merged batch causes p95 increase > 10% for any tenant. Also requested canary bucket with 'no-merge' traffic to compare.

2026-01-21 | Diego Alvarez: Implemented PoC for merge window (4ms) in ingress aggregator. PoC merged to feature branch: perf/opportunistic-merge. Initial local perf shows average batch size increase 1.9x for our microbench workload. Pushed PR #7123 for early review.

2026-01-25 | Erika Liu (Security): Security review: no additional data flow risk seen as hints are metadata only. Confirmed RBAC controls for background KV rebalance. Security approval recorded in Confluence.

2026-01-27 | Diego Alvarez: Started KV hinting PR. We decided to encode a 16-bit locality token in request metadata to avoid expanding envelope size. PR #7160 opened. Noted compatibility shim for older clients that won't send hints.

2026-01-29 | Benchmarks (perf infra bot): Canary simulation (1M requests over 1 hour) in us-west2: baseline p99=142ms, opportunistic merge p99=124ms (-12.6%). Cross-shard KV fetches down 24%. GPU throughput increased by 18% under small-batch load. Details in Grafana link.

2026-02-01 | Andrea Novak (PM): PM review: Confirm that rollout plan includes Dedicated tenants on a separate opt-in path, and that docs explain the effect on latency SLOs. Added task to update SDK changelog.

2026-02-02 | Diego Alvarez: Raised a follow-up ticket suggestion to evaluate adaptive merge-window (machine-learned) if static windows are insufficient. Marking this ticket ready for final code review and SRE canary scheduling.
